Before Phase 3: source-reading targets r2_capture.main and r2_capture.observe, not probe-scan choices. main captures only its controlled scalar result dictionary: failed, error_number, test_ms, startup_ms, ready, port, body_bytes, status, reset, request_ms. observe allowlists kind, port, body_bytes, status, reset, elapsed_ms. No Request/response objects, raw URL, exception text, planted payload or host attributes captured. No generic urllib probes; exporter traffic is excluded by the test-private facade. Readiness timing is not actual Go bind timing/port ownership, which remain unknown.
Outer investigation recorder and collector OMIT capture_policy/capture_profile (legacy mode), because strict Policy.envelope unconditionally drops semantic IDs and queued policy drops manifest bookkeeping. This explicitly leaves P0 strict mode for this synthetic-only outer recording. The privacy test's own producer and server still run their unchanged strict P0 policy. This is not privacy-safe for real data. Explicit capture fields and controlled scalars are the capture boundary here. Defaults: queue 256 items, no extra queue options unless drops. Required --doctor --manifest --drain-timeout 30. One test body per recording invocation, at most 20 (budget remainder), stop early at >=5 failures and >=5 passes. No pilot test-body runs.
